chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about eating locusts, so he said, 'There is no harm in eating it.' Then he said, 'It is a scattering of fish in the sea.' Then he said, 'Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Locusts and fish, when they come out of the water, are slaughtered (dhabihah); the land is a slaughter-ground for locusts, and for fish it is also so.''
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating locusts in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to establish the permissibility of locusts (*jarad*) without ritual slaughter, a view widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of 'a handful of fish from the sea' to emphasize their natural purity, while attributing to Imam Ali (peace be upon him) the legal reasoning that their transition from water to land or air renders them lawful (*dhabihah*) by virtue of their exit from their natural element.
